concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper bound on growth rate.

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Sums of powers of a variable with coefficients.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a+bi with i²=-1, including roots of unity.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed finite number of one-dimensional tapes; running time counts steps.

concepts.name: Convolution and cyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: Combining two coefficient lists so entry k sums products of entries whose indices add to k (cyclically modulo the length in the cyclic case); this is polynomial multiplication.

evidence.quote: Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Fourier transform and roots of unity
concepts.gloss: The discrete Fourier transform evaluates a coefficient list at powers of a root of unity, turning convolution into pointwise product; fast algorithms compute it in layers of two-point butterflies.

evidence.quote:
the transform calculation consists of address
rearrangements, signed shifts, and two-point butterfly operations

concepts.name: The n log n optimality conjecture
concepts.gloss: Schönhage and Strassen's 1971 O(n log n log log n) multitape multiplication and their proposal that n log n is optimal; Harvey and van der Hoeven later reached O(n log n).

evidence.quote: and proposed $n\log n$ as the optimal order of growth

Harvey and van der Hoeven reached the unconditional $O(n\log n)$ upper
bound

concepts.name: Multiplication as radix-digit convolution
concepts.gloss: Split each integer into short radix digits so the product becomes a convolution of integer coefficient lists; carries then give the exact product.

evidence.quote:
Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to
convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Arrays on tapes, scans and stored bit volume
concepts.gloss: Data is stored as arrays addressed by fields of bits in a fixed order on tapes; elementary scans and stream operations cost time linear in the stored bit volume.

evidence.quote:
Scanning an array of $\Theta(n)$ stored bits at each of
$\Theta(\log n)$ transform levels already costs $\Theta(n\log n)$.

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: polynomial variable
symbols.meaning: The formal variable of the polynomials; its powers serve as roots of unity.

symbols.name: coefficient count
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a record, a power of two.

concepts.gloss: Complex polynomials in y of degree below r multiplied with y^r replaced by -1; powers of y act as roots of unity, so multiplying by one is a signed cyclic shift of the coefficient list.

evidence.quote:
one coordinate
is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$, with $r$ a power of two

multiplication by
such a root is a signed shift of the coefficient list

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transforms
concepts.gloss: Fourier-type transforms over the ring modulo y^r+1 that use powers of y as roots of unity, so each transform consists of address rearrangements, signed shifts and butterflies (Nussbaumer; Quandalle and Nussbaumer).

evidence.quote:
These are the
synthetic polynomial transforms of Nussbaumer and Quandalle and
Nussbaumer

concepts.name: Controlled shifts and carries by packing
concepts.gloss: Elementary tape procedures that shift records by amounts given by control values, used to implement signed shifts and address maps.

evidence.quote:
Those changes are implemented by whole-chunk moves and
controlled shifts

concepts.name: Signed coefficient packing (Kronecker substitution) and the n log n subroutine
concepts.gloss: Polynomial products over the ring are computed by packing signed coefficients into long integers and calling the established O(n log n) multiplier as an ordinary subroutine.

evidence.quote:
Their polynomial products
use signed packing and the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier as an
ordinary subroutine.

Signed coefficient
packing is a form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder map onto prime cyclic axes
concepts.gloss: A map placing the radix-digit coefficient list on a product of distinct prime cyclic axes that preserves convolution, implemented by triangular controlled shifts and axis moves.

evidence.quote:
the radix-digit coefficient list is placed on a product of
distinct prime cyclic axes by a Chinese-remainder map that preserves
convolution

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: Harvey and van der Hoeven's identity expressing each Fourier transform of prime length through a multidimensional transform with power-of-two axis lengths; source and target permutations stay inside the identity instead of being executed as sorts.

evidence.quote:
Gaussian
resampling then expresses each source Fourier transform through a
power-of-two tensor transform.

retains the
source and target coordinate permutations in the transform identity

concepts.name: Bluestein chirp conversion
concepts.gloss: Bluestein's chirp identity rewrites a Fourier transform as a convolution with chirp factors, so the middle transform with its target permutation becomes a normalized cyclic convolution.

evidence.quote:
Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform,
including its target permutation, into normalized cyclic convolution.

concepts.name: Last-coordinate phase twist
concepts.gloss: A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial modulo y^r+1, whose negative wrap gives the original cyclic wrap once the twist is removed.

evidence.quote:
A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial
modulo $y^r+1$

concepts.name: Linear networks with roles and frames
concepts.gloss: A fixed linear network of scalar gates exchanging banks of values and restoring auxiliary values is applied to row streams, one role per wire; a frame is an invertible operator giving the stored representation, and intermediate frames cancel leaving an endpoint operator.

evidence.quote: A wire's fixed place in the network is called its role.

We call $D_v$ its frame: the stored
array is $D_vg$ when the logical array is $g$.

concepts.name: Restoring auxiliary values
concepts.gloss: Scratch registers with arbitrary initial contents are subtracted, used, added back and the computation reversed, so every auxiliary value is restored (transparent computation).

evidence.quote:
Restoring scratch registers with arbitrary initial contents also has a
precise precedent.

concepts.name: Finite network from three-element subsets
concepts.gloss: A fixed small network built from three-element subsets of an m-dimensional ground set, with gather, scatter and auxiliary wires cancelling unwanted coefficients, assigning nested subspaces to gates so the number s of smaller calls satisfies s<Wm.

evidence.quote:
The construction uses
three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients depending
on intersection size, and auxiliary wires cancel the unwanted
coefficients.

The decisive property is that the total
number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.

concepts.name: Recursive power saving
concepts.gloss: A recursive call at parameter mf uses s<Wm calls at parameter f on streams of volume V/W, so dividing by volume the cost grows by factor s/W<m per multiplication of the parameter by m, giving a power rather than a logarithmic saving.

evidence.quote:
This strict inequality
is the source of the power saving.

concepts.name: Address shear and lower triangular factorization
concepts.gloss: The endpoint operator of the bit network updates two address fields by (H,D)↦(H+D,D); rank reduction via a Bruhat-type factorization into lower-triangular matrices makes such shears cheap on tape.

evidence.quote:
two fields, written as vectors $H,D$ over a common residue ring, are
updated by $(H,D)\mapsto(H+D,D)$

concepts.name: Fast address-field interchange
concepts.title: Fast interchange of address fields in cost $O(Vu^\tau)$

symbols.name: stored bit volume
symbols.meaning: The total number of bits stored in the array.

symbols.name: field width
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each interchanged address field.

symbols.name: interchange exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed constant below 1 giving the power saving in the field width.

concepts.gloss: Interchanging two disjoint contiguous address fields of u bits in a Cartesian-product array at cost O(V u^τ) for a fixed τ<1, via intermediate XOR combinations whose final effect is an exact permutation.

evidence.quote: Its cost is $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$.

Although its final effect is an exact permutation, its intermediate
steps form pointwise XOR combinations of data.

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer
concepts.title: Simultaneous butterfly layers in cost $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$

symbols.name: stored bit volume
symbols.meaning: The total number of bits stored in the numerical arrays.

symbols.name: chunk count
symbols.meaning: The number of equal-width address chunks in which one bit position is selected.

symbols.name: butterfly exponent
symbols.meaning: A fixed constant below 1 giving the power saving in the number of selected chunks.

concepts.gloss: The map H₀(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u−v)/2) applied coefficientwise to polynomial records at one chosen bit position in each of d address chunks at cost O(V d^λ′), using exact Gaussian dyadic intermediates and one truncation afterward.

evidence.quote:
The second procedure applies
\[
 H_0(u,v)=\bigl((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2\bigr)
\]

the cost is $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ for a
fixed $\lambda'<1$

concepts.name: Synthetic transform layout and convolution
concepts.gloss: Forward synthetic transforms keep the same frequency order through the pointwise product and the opposite transform consumes it, so convolution over the ring is computed on the retained layout using fast butterfly layers and address interchanges.

evidence.quote:
The two forward synthetic transforms
retain the same frequency order through their pointwise product, and
the opposite transform consumes that order.

concepts.name: Precision, rounding and carry propagation
concepts.gloss: After removing known normalizations and digit scales, the recovered coefficient error is shown strictly below 1/2, so rounding gives exact integer coefficients and carries yield the binary product.

evidence.quote:
proves that the recovered
coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$, and propagates carries to
obtain the exact binary product

concepts.name: Integer multiplication in O(n (lg n)^(1−κ)) time
concepts.title: Integer multiplication in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time

symbols.name: bit length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits of each input integer.

symbols.name: binary logarithm
symbols.meaning: The base-2 logarithm rounded up, at least 1.

symbols.name: saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed constant 2^-182 giving the power saving in the logarithmic factor.

concepts.gloss: A deterministic multitape Turing machine multiplies n-bit integers in O(n(lg n)^(1−κ)) time with κ=2^−182, by chaining digit convolution, Chinese-remainder map, Gaussian resampling, chirps, twist, and synthetic transforms accelerated by fast interchanges and butterfly layers.

evidence.quote:
disproves the $n\log n$ optimality conjecture
of Sch\"onhage and Strassen in this model

We obtain a strict power saving in the
logarithmic factor, in the same fixed finite-tape model.

concepts.name: Logarithms and iterated logarithms
concepts.gloss: The base-2 logarithm lg n is the exponent to which 2 is raised to get n, and lg lg n applies it twice.

concepts.name: Binary representation of integers
concepts.gloss: A nonnegative integer below 2^n is written as a string of n bits, the coefficients of its powers of 2.

concepts.name: Positional radix notation
concepts.gloss: An integer is written as a sum of digits times powers of a base, so splitting into digits and recombining with carries are inverse operations.

concepts.name: Schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication
concepts.gloss: Schoolbook multiplication takes quadratic time in the bit length, and Karatsuba's divide-and-conquer multiplication improves this to a power below 2.

concepts.name: Recursion and divide-and-conquer recurrences
concepts.gloss: Running time of a recursive algorithm is described by a recurrence that is solved by unrolling levels or by the master theorem.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Integers are compared and combined modulo n, so indices and values wrap around cyclically.

concepts.name: Primes and coprimality
concepts.gloss: A prime has no divisors besides 1 and itself, and integers with gcd 1 are coprime.

concepts.name: Chinese remainder theorem
concepts.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli, residues modulo each determine a unique residue modulo their product, giving an isomorphism of Z/(m1...mk) with the product of the Z/mi.

concepts.name: Permutations and bijections
concepts.gloss: A permutation is a bijective rearrangement of a list of positions, and sorting realizes one.

concepts.name: Vectors, matrices and linear maps
concepts.gloss: Linear maps are represented by matrices acting on coefficient vectors, compose by matrix product, and are undone by inverses.

concepts.name: Subspaces, dimension and linear independence
concepts.gloss: A subspace is a subset of a vector space closed under linear combination, with a dimension given by the size of a basis.

concepts.name: Triangular matrices and Gaussian elimination
concepts.gloss: Triangular matrices have zeros on one side of the diagonal, and Gaussian elimination factors or inverts matrices by elementary row operations.

concepts.name: Bitwise operations and XOR
concepts.gloss: XOR adds bits modulo 2, and fields of bits in a binary address can be read and modified independently.

concepts.name: Cartesian products and multidimensional arrays
concepts.gloss: A multidimensional array is indexed by tuples from a product of finite sets, and can be laid out linearly by an ordering of indices.

concepts.name: Sets and subsets
concepts.gloss: A subset consists of chosen elements of a ground set, and the number of subsets of a given size is counted combinatorially.

concepts.name: Rationals, rounding and error bounds
concepts.gloss: Real approximations are rounded to the nearest integer, which is exact when the total error is strictly below 1/2 and is bounded by summing individual errors.

concepts.name: Dyadic rationals and fixed-point numbers
concepts.gloss: A dyadic rational has a power of 2 as denominator and is stored as an integer scaled by a power of 2.

concepts.name: Two's complement and signed integers
concepts.gloss: Negative integers are stored in binary through a sign convention such as two's complement, with offsets or sign bits.

concepts.name: Basic ring and group structure
concepts.gloss: A commutative ring has addition and multiplication satisfying the usual laws, and it can be quotiented by a relation such as y^r = -1.

concepts.name: Euler's formula and primitive roots of unity
concepts.gloss: The number e^{2 pi i/N} is a primitive N-th root of unity of modulus 1, and its powers are the points evenly spaced on the unit circle.

concepts.name: Fast Fourier transform for power-of-two length
concepts.gloss: The radix-2 FFT computes a length-2^k transform in O(N log N) arithmetic operations by splitting recursively into half-length transforms and combining with butterflies.

concepts.name: Gaussian function
concepts.gloss: The function exp(-pi x^2) is a rapidly decaying bell-shaped function whose tails give small approximation errors.

concepts.name: Time and space as functions of input size
concepts.gloss: Algorithms are compared by worst-case step counts as functions of input length, and a subroutine is used as a black box with its running time.

concepts.name: Tape head movement and sequential access
concepts.gloss: A Turing machine head moves one cell per step, so scanning a tape costs time proportional to its length and random access is not free.

background.summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education: asymptotic analysis, recursion and divide-and-conquer recurrences, basic discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, primes, Chinese remainder theorem, permutations, sets), and introductory linear algebra (vectors, matrices, invertible maps, subspaces, triangular matrices, Gaussian elimination). They know binary arithmetic, schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication, and basic Turing machines with tapes. They have not studied abstract algebra beyond basics, the FFT in depth, Schönhage-Strassen, Nussbaumer transforms, or fast multitape tape-programming techniques; those are explained by the wiki.
